name: Tu Mu
bio: Tu Mu (AD 803–852) was a late T’ang poet, known for polished quatrains on history, travel and love.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Lost Love
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.text:
Too late, alas! I came to find the lovely spring had fled.
Yet must I not regret the days of youth that now are dead;
For though the rosy buds of spring the cruel winds have laid,
Behold the clustering fruit that hangs beneath the leafy shade!

poems.title: The Old Place
poems.author: Tu Mu

poems.title: The Last Night
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.text:
Old love would seem as though not love today;
Spell-bound by thee, my laughter dies away.
The very wax sheds sympathetic tears
And gutters sadly down till dawn appears.

poems.title: Lovers Parted
poems.author: Tu Mu
poems.text:
Across the screen the autumn moon stares coldly from the sky;
With silken fan I sit and flick the fireflies sailing by.
The night grows colder every hour, — it chills me to the heart
To watch the Spinning Maiden from the Herdboy far apart.
